data_quality_notes:
Research ran to completion — notes.md carries a RESEARCH COMPLETE block, so `truncated` is false and nothing here is reconstructed from fragments. 8 captured lines, 7 unique ideas (SMH appears twice; the later line supersedes it with the stop disclosure and size cut from 3% to 2%).

WHAT THE IDEA COUNT MEANS. All seven are swing and four of seven are position closes (LCII, NKE, CEG, TLT). That is stated rather than apologised for: a 16-position book with a 1/7 hit rate and four unstopped or noise-stopped losers needed exits more than it needed new risk this morning. Only three ideas are new. No intraday idea (the market was shut all weekend; there was no live equity tape). No long_term idea, and that is the deliberate gap worth flagging — a long_term call needs a defended valuation anchor and a bear-case price, and market_data.py exposes no fundamentals (no earnings power, book value, FCF or multiple). Silver was tested on both the swing and long clocks and failed both; ACN, COST and the power complex were examined as de-ratings and rejected on fetched evidence. The only valuation anchor buildable all run was LCII's, and it existed because a merger fixed the exchange ratio. Nothing was manufactured to fill the lane.

PRICES. Every equity and ETF price is the 2026-09-18 close, fetched with session 'pre' and an age of ~3,749 minutes. At 06:00 ET Monday with the market shut that is the freshest honest price, not stale data. Crypto (BTC 84,599) is the only genuinely live price in this run and it is on the watchlist, not in a recommendation.

SOURCES THAT FAILED. Yahoo returned HTTP 429 on every index, FX and commodity symbol (^GSPC, ^NDX, ^DJI, ^RUT, ^VIX, ES=F, NQ=F, DX-Y.NYB, ^TNX, GC=F, CL=F), so there is NO VIX, dollar, futures, gold or crude print anywhere in this report — liquid ETF proxies via finnhub are used instead and named as such, and market_context.levels carries null for what could not be fetched rather than an estimate. yahoo-options returned HTTP 401 on every symbol, so the SMH 671.83 and XRT 77.86 targets were NOT checked against the options-implied move that config/strategy.md requires; this is carried in each idea's counter_argument rather than passed over silently. Kalshi returned 0 markets across five macro queries, so no event contract could be priced or re-checked — including the three sitting in 'awaiting entry', two of which reference a September Fed decision that has now happened. api.nasdaq.com `short` timed out twice, so there is no short-interest or days-to-cover read on any name, which matters most for the XRT short. Working: FRED, finnhub (quotes, earnings calendar, insiders, analysts), nasdaq history/ATR/SMA, SEC EDGAR, coingecko standalone.

ARITHMETIC. Every ratio was recomputed at synthesis from the final entry, target and stop against a freshly fetched ATR14, not carried over from the notes: XRT 2.459 (1.88 ATR, ETF floor 1.8), KMX 2.924 (2.37 ATR, stock floor 2.0), SMH 3.327 (1.87 ATR, ETF floor 1.8). All three clear both floors. The spread 2.46 / 2.92 / 3.33 is deliberately not the just-above-2.0 cluster that signals targets fitted to the bar, and all three targets are measured 150-day range extremes rather than constructed numbers. Claimed edge over the 1/(1+R:R) break-even is +9.1, +10.5 and +9.9 points respectively — real but modest, and none large enough to need a bigger thesis to carry it.

TWO DISCLOSURES THE RED TEAM SHOULD SEE RATHER THAN REDISCOVER. (1) SMH is borderline and is ranked first anyway. Its 555.00 stop is 1.87 ATR, clearing the 1.8 ETF floor by 0.07; the structurally safer stop below the 537.73 base low is 3.11 ATR but leaves R:R at 1.996, a hair UNDER the 2.0 swing floor, so the wide-stop version does not publish at all. The tighter stop giving the better ratio is exactly the tell this repo documents on KRE. It was derived independently — below the 09-17 low, below the 20d SMA, below the base midpoint — and the mitigations are size cut to 2%, the full calculation in key_risk, and the missing options check named. If one idea is cut today it should be this one. (2) XRT's conviction is 3, not the 4 its three distinct evidence kinds would score. It was discounted on purpose because the dated catalyst is AZO's print, a read-across to XRT rather than XRT's own event. Under-claiming is the safe direction.

DECLARED CONFLICT, NOT AN ERROR. KMX long and XRT short point opposite ways at the same cohort. XRT is the retail basket, lagging SPY on every window; KMX is the one name beating that basket by 33.78% over 6m with the only clean multi-buyer, zero-sell insider cluster found across 22 names. Long the divergence, short the aggregate reduces net consumer exposure rather than doubling it, and neither idea needs the other to be right. Correlation cap respected: no more than 3 ideas depend on any one driver.

NOT REACHED: healthcare/biotech beyond the XBI level, financials beyond KRE, international ex-EEM, and any systematic small-cap screen — small caps were reachable only through the earnings calendar, which is a narrow door.

RED TEAM (phase 2c). Cut 2 of 7, downgraded 1, re-ranked the rest; 5 remain. Every number below was recomputed from a freshly fetched ATR14 and SMA set, not read off the report.

CUT SMH (was rank 1, conviction 4). Its own disclosure was correct and is the reason: the 555.00 stop is the tightest placement clearing the 1.8 ETF floor, at no fetched level, and the structural stop below the 537.73 base low gives 1.996:1 — under the swing floor. A ratio that exists only at a fitted stop is the KRE artifact, so the trade never cleared the bar. The 6.22-ATR target against a 6.0 guide compounds it.

CUT XRT (was rank 5, conviction 3), on an error the report made twice rather than on judgement: evidence and counter_argument both state the 87.20 stop sits above the broken 50d SMA, and the 50d SMA is 87.8334 — the stop is 0.63 below the level whose reclaim the report itself calls the invalidation, so the short stops out before its thesis is disproved. Placed honestly above the 50d the ratio is 1.84:1, and 1.988:1 even a cent above it. The 2.46:1 was never available. The consumer read-across thesis survives on the watchlist; the levels did not.

KMX 4 to 3, kept at rank 5. It survives because its stop is the one of the three at structure — 48.80 below the 49.37 60-day range low, 2.37 ATR, clearing the 2.0 stock floor unaided — and because a target pulled in to the 6.0 ATR guide still gives 2.53:1. Downgraded because two of its three evidence kinds are backward-looking (June insider buys, 6-month relative strength) against a rate shock the report concedes it cannot price, and because cutting XRT removed the short leg of the declared pair: the same position is now an outright consumer long rather than the hedged divergence it was scored as. Conviction should follow the risk it actually carries.

KEPT ALL FOUR POSITION CLOSES (NKE, CEG, LCII, TLT) and re-ranked them above the one new idea, because each is actionable at today's open while KMX cannot trigger until after 09-29. Their 'fail' verdicts are mechanical artifacts of the close shape, not defects: direction_consistency, risk_reward and stop_distance all fail for want of a target and stop, which a full exit does not have. LCII's parity arithmetic was re-verified independently (PATK 68.71 x 1.2440 = 85.4752 against LCII 85.60, a 0.15% premium — no spread left to hold for). CEG's catalyst was undated and is now stamped 2026-09-21T09:30, matching its own stated action of closing at Monday's open. LCII's and TLT's catalysts are dated in the past and were left that way: for a close, a catalyst that has already resolved is the reason to act, not an error to tidy.

TWO VALIDATION FLAGS CHECKED AND DISMISSED. The earnings_date warn fired on four ideas claiming an earnings catalyst; all six dated catalysts in this report (MU 09-30, KMX 09-29, NKE 09-28, COST 09-24, AZO 09-22, KBH 09-22) were re-fetched from the finnhub calendar and every one confirms, so the warn is a lookup artifact. KMX's spread FAIL (bid 57.27 / ask 61.40 = 6.96%) is an out-of-hours quote artifact, not a tradability finding — the same fetch prints a 45.4% spread on LCII, which is not a real market in a $2.1B S&P name at 06:34 on a Monday with the exchange shut. KMX turns over $99M a day; the entry is a limit order placed after 09-29 and the spread is checkable at fill time. Neither flag changed a decision.

NOT CUT AND WORTH SAYING PLAINLY: the two kills are the same defect found twice, not a quota. Both had a stop placed to clear a floor instead of to mark where the thesis is wrong, and in both cases moving the stop to the level the report itself named dropped the ratio below 2.0. KMX had the same warn on its stop_distance and passed the same test, which is why it is still here. What remains is an honest morning: four exits that reduce risk today, and one conditional entry a week out. Validation demoted 5 idea(s) whose numbers did not check out. 0 more carry warnings — see the validation block on each.

market_context.summary:
The Fed HIKED 25bp on 2026-09-17 — effective fed funds 3.63% to 3.88%, verified in FRED rather than assumed — into 4.1% unemployment and a firm CPI (+0.40% m/m NSA in August). The informative part is what the bond market did with it: both 2s and 10s FELL through the hike (10y 5.01% to 4.94%, 2y 4.74% to 4.67%), so the market is reading the move as growth-restrictive rather than inflation-permissive. That takes long-duration bonds off the obvious-short list and is why the TLT short is being covered.

The tape is one market in two halves. Mega-cap tech led Friday (QQQ +0.63%) while breadth was poor (SPY -0.12%, IWM -0.47%), and of twenty sector baskets fetched only XLK and SMH trade above both their 20d and 50d averages. Everything rate-sensitive or consumer-facing — ITB, IYR, XLI, KRE, XLB, XLU (-1.42%, the worst of the ten majors) — is below both.

The single most coherent signal is a cohort, not a name: seven fetched consumer-facing names and six of them within 7% of a 150-day low (CCL +0.1% above its low, NKE +0.03%, COST +0.8%, AZO +1.4%, LULU +2.8%, KBH +7.0%), into a Fed that just tightened. That argues against bargain-hunting the cohort rather than for it, and the two broken consumer longs already on the book (NKE -11.2%, LULU -14.7%) are the evidence that catching this knife has cost money once already. The one honest exception is KMX, which is beating the basket with insiders buying — hence long the divergence, short the aggregate.

One unresolved divergence worth naming: precious metals ROSE through the hike (SLV +1.63%, the best of the ten majors; GLD +0.71%), which a pure real-rate story does not predict. It was worked hard and priced on neither the swing nor the long clock, so it sits on the watchlist rather than in a recommendation.

watchlist.note: Red team CUT from rank 1. The 3.33:1 ratio is an artifact of a stop fitted to the floor rather than to structure — the KRE failure mode this repo documents. The 555.00 stop is 1.87 ATR, the tightest placement that clears the 1.8 ETF floor (a stop below the 20d SMA at 557.82 would be 1.73 ATR and fail it outright), and it sits at no fetched level. The structural stop below the 537.73 base low is 537.00 = 3.11 ATR, and at that honest distance reward-to-risk is 89.83/45.00 = 1.996 — under the 2.0 swing floor. There is therefore no version of this trade with a defensible stop that clears the bar; the published version exists only because the stop was moved in. Compounding it, the 671.83 target is the exact 150-day range high, 6.22 ATR from entry against a 6.0 ATR swing guide with 15 sessions to run, on a basket that is -13.17% over 3m and lagging SPY by 15.17% — and the options-implied move could not be checked (yahoo-options HTTP 401). Synthesis flagged this itself and said if one idea were cut it should be this one. Agreed, and the arithmetic was re-derived from a fresh ATR14 of 14.4517 rather than taken from the report.
watchlist.trigger: a pullback deep enough that a stop below the 537.73 base low still clears 2.0:1, or a breakout above 580.81 that establishes a nearer measured target than the 150-day high

watchlist.note: Red team CUT from rank 5, on a defect the report did not catch. The 87.20 stop is described twice — in the technical_level evidence and again in counter_argument — as sitting 'above the broken 50d SMA'. It does not. The 50d SMA is 87.8334 (refetched this run), so the stop is 0.63 BELOW the very level whose reclaim counter_argument names as the thesis invalidation: the short is stopped out before its own invalidation is reached, which is a stop placed in noise rather than at structure, and 87.20 corresponds to nothing fetched. Put the stop where the report says it already is and the ratio collapses — at 88.10 (above the 50d) risk is 3.60 = 2.50 ATR and reward-to-risk is 6.64/3.60 = 1.84; even at 87.84, one cent above the SMA, it is 1.988. No honest placement clears the 2.0 floor, so the published 2.46:1 never existed. The read-across thesis itself (a tightening Fed into a consumer cohort at 150-day lows) is intact and is what to re-derive from — the level set is what failed, not the idea.
